obligations.note: POST /payees/{id}/reopen is bound to privileged action manage_payees with mfa=False, and app.py enforces MFA only when route.mfa is true. The exhaustive control test failed on that route, and EXC-0237 does not excuse it because Sofia Santos approved her own request and is not a risk_owner.
reopen_payee updates only status and closed_at. NPI columns are still written through Vault.seal, and test_every_npi_field_is_sealed_at_rest passed.

reopen_payee calls _audit with the actor, action reopen_payee, target payee id, and clock time after the update. The other state-changing methods in service.py do the same, and the sampled audit control test passed.
The new UPDATE is a fixed SQL string with the payee id bound as a parameter. The rest of store.py uses the same pattern, and test_sql_statements_are_parameterized passed.
Ticket CHG-25323 is standard, approved by change manager Grace Kim on 2026-10-22, before review, and its components cover payments.http, routes, service, and store.
Mara Costa, a payments change_approver and not the author, approved a code_review of commit fd18083e7bcb.
The change is a single commit, and both the code review and the security review name that commit.
records/ci/run.json records result failure on the head commit. The registered MFA-1 control test is unskipped and failing, so the full suite did not pass.
The change touches security-sensitive routes, app, and store. Kofi Mensah, a security_reviewer and not the author, approved a security_review of the head commit.
The diff does not touch controls data, control tests, or CI, so no control-owner approval is required.
The ticket type is standard and the change is not marked emergency, so a post-implementation review is not due.
EXC-0237 is the cited MFA-1 exception for payments.routes, but it was approved by requester Sofia Santos, who does not hold the risk_owner role.
Acceptance record ACR-0404 covers routes.py for MFA-1, and this change alters that file. The replacement exhaustive control test on the head commit failed, so the lapsed evidence was not replaced.

summary: The new reopen route uses privileged action manage_payees without MFA, and the app only checks the route flag. The cited exception was approved by the requester, who is not a CISO risk owner, so it does not waive MFA-1. CI on the head commit failed the exhaustive privileged-route control test, which also lapses the prior MFA-1 acceptance record. Encryption, audit of the new operation, parameterized SQL, and the other change-process records are in order, but the MFA break, the invalid exception, and the failed suite require rejection.
